_comment: Copy this file to sqreader.config.json (gitignored) and edit as needed.
Every value here is a DEFAULT; a matching CLI flag always wins over it.
On a standard single-instance box you usually need NO config at all: the
Squad server is found by its process name and output dirs default next to
the repo. Only non-standard setups need to change anything below.
The file is loaded from $SQREADER_CONFIG, else ./sqreader.config.json.
_seeding_comment: Matches the game names with one of these modes are never recorded: no
.sqrx, no stats row, no upload. Seeding is what this is for - a two-
player six-hour warm-up arrives in the archive dressed as a match and
drags every average it touches down with it. Matched EXACTLY and case-
insensitively against the mode the game reports; set to [] on a box whose
whole purpose is testing against seed layers.
seeding_layer_patterns is the override hatch for matches whose mode is a
normal one but which are still not real play - scrims, events, training.
Case-insensitive fnmatch globs against the layer name (map name if no
layer resolved), e.g. ["*Skirmish*"]. Empty by default: a pattern that is
too broad loses real matches, and silently.
Cheat detection is deliberately NOT gated on this - plugins keep running
through a seed session, because that is when a bored cheater tries things.
_plugins_comment: Plugins are off unless a config path is given. --plugins-config wins;
this key is the fallback for deployments whose start command is not
yours to edit. The file it points at is {plugin_id: {enabled, config}}.
_alerts_comment: Plugin alerts (see --plugins-config) always land in the stats database.
Set alert_webhook to a Discord webhook URL to have them announced there
as well. That URL is a CREDENTIAL - anyone holding it can post in the
channel - which is why it lives here and not on a command line other
users on the box can read out of `ps`.
alert_replay_base builds a 'watch the replay' link on each alert; without
it the alert still arrives, just with no way to go and look.
alert_min_confidence keeps the noisy end of a detector in the database
without putting it in a channel humans are expected to read.
_multi_instance_comment: Running SEVERAL Squad servers on one box? Set squad_port to the -Port= of
the one THIS agent reads, and give each agent its own server_id. Without
it the server is found by process name, which answers with an arbitrary
one of them — so every agent may end up reading the same game, and which
game that is can change on any restart. Each instance also needs its own
install dir, HTTP port and systemd unit: see the installer's
_push_comment: Optional central push (OFF by default). Report FINISHED matches (stats +
.sqrx replays; never the live map) to a central platform. Enroll first:
is stored in a 0600 .env.agent, NOT here. See PRIVACY.md.
push_replay: also upload the match replay (set false for stats-only).
push_backlog_dir: pending-push queue (default: next to the stats DB).
